paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God hears everything. Mount Seir (where Esau, also called Edom, settled) kept running its mouth about Israel's mountains, saying, "They are desolate; they are given to us to devour!" God says, "I heard it Myself!" (Ezekiel 35:12-13). So the people who laughed when God's people were down were not getting away with anything, and God was never looking the other way.

Now the other half, and it's the good half. God's word to Mount Seir was "Behold, I am against you," but to the mountains of Israel He says, "For behold, I am on your side" (Ezekiel 35:3, 36:9). Israel's mountains had been trampled, mocked and talked about by the nations. God says they will bear fruit, the ruins will be rebuilt, and His people will soon come home (Ezekiel 36:8-11). When your situation looks like a pile of rubble, friend, that's not the last word, because God's word is the last word.

So what do you do with this, baker? When somebody laughs at you or counts you out, you don't have to fire back. God has heard every word, and He keeps His promises to His people. He says, "Then you will know that I am the LORD" (Ezekiel 36:11). Trust Him with the mocking, the mess and the waiting, and keep your oven warm.
